## Natural history notes

A large big-headed ant characterized by two worker forms, with smaller minor workers and much larger major workers that have oversized heads and strong mandibles. In Florida, it is found in disturbed open habitats, lawns, parks, roadsides, gardens, fields, and urban or suburban areas where colonies nest in soil, under debris, or near pavement and structures. It forages for small insects, seeds, honeydew, carrion, and other food sources, often forming conspicuous trails and competing with native ants in human-modified landscapes.
